summary: Iteration 18 — End-to-end verification of Phase 2B: Turnstile CAPTCHA gate, wallet redesign (WalletPanel with hero + presets + custom amount + filters + receipt modal), attempts-per-ticket pool enforcement, and Admin EditContestDialog attempts_per_ticket field. Backend: 8/9 new pytest tests pass — ONE critical Stripe 500 on the new /api/payments/wallet-topup/custom endpoint (missing tax_code on inline price_data). Frontend: all wallet UI, TurnstileGate auto-pass, and Admin EditContestDialog checks green.

critical.issue: Returns 500 for valid £5 top-up. Stripe rejects with `Invalid line_items[0]: the product tax code is missing. You must set the product's tax_code to one eligible for Managed Payments.` — the inline `price_data.product_data` has no `tax_code`. Fallback path (automatic_tax + billing_address_collection) also fails with `You must specify a tax code in all line items to calculate taxes`. The legacy /wallet-topup/checkout endpoint works because pre-configured Prices already have the tax code attached. FIX: add `"tax_code": "txcd_10103001"` (or another digital tax code) inside `product_data`, or drop managed_payments/automatic_tax for custom sessions.

ui_bugs.issue: Hero card shows `Attempts left: 3/3` — hardcoded (`const attemptsLeft = 3 - attempts.length`). Should reflect pooled attempts (tickets_owned × attempts_per_ticket) coming from /api/orders/my-games or the /api/games/submit response. UI-only cosmetic — enforcement is server-side and works.

action_items: Fix /api/payments/wallet-topup/custom Stripe tax_code — add `"tax_code": "txcd_10103001"` inside `line_items[0].price_data.product_data` (or move to a non-managed / non-automatic-tax session for custom amounts). This blocks the £5 preset and custom-amount top-ups from the WalletPanel UI. Repro: `curl -X POST $API/payments/wallet-topup/custom -H 'Authorization: Bearer <token>' -d '{"amount":5.0,"origin_url":"https://example.com"}'` → 500.
PlayGame.jsx: replace hardcoded `Attempts left: 3/3` with pooled attempts from /api/orders/my-games (attempts_remaining / max_attempts). Optional but user-facing.

Consider min £5 alignment across surface: `/api/wallet/topup` (mock player top-up) still has MIN_TOPUP=£10 in wallet_routes.py — new UI advertises min £5 everywhere. Not user-hit today (mock endpoint is not called by WalletPanel) but drift will bite later.
critical_code_review_comments: MyAccount.jsx is 663 lines — still over the 700-line soft limit warning; wallet tab is now cleanly extracted to WalletPanel.jsx, so continuing the split (Profile / KYC / Referrals / Preferences into their own files) would keep it healthy.

PlayGame.jsx still uses `contestsAPI.list()` and filters by contest_id client-side to find the current contest. Two issues: (1) list() only returns LIVE contests, so a contest paused mid-session breaks the play page; (2) fetches N contests to find 1. Prefer a dedicated `GET /api/contests/{contest_id}` endpoint (or /api/games/contest/{id}).

TurnstileGate: on `enabled=true && site_key` present, if the Cloudflare script fails to load (blocked / offline), the widget never renders and the user has no way to submit — component polls forever. Add a 15s timeout that surfaces an error toast with a Retry button.

captcha_routes.py: `verify_challenge_token` compares user + contest but the /api/games/submit path doesn't gate the check when `TEST_OTP_BYPASS_CODE` is set (line 102: `and not os.environ.get('TEST_OTP_BYPASS_CODE')`). That's convenient for tests but means anyone knowing the env has a bypass. Fine for preview, but production must drop TEST_OTP_BYPASS_CODE.

payments_routes.py: `_apply_tx` is invoked inside `_credit_wallet_once` even after an update_one sets `wallet_credited`; if two webhooks arrive concurrently a race could still double-credit. Consider a Mongo unique index on `(session_id)` for the credit doc or a `$set:{wallet_credited:true}` conditional update inside `_apply_tx`.

order_routes.py my-games: `tickets_owned = sum(1 for t2 in tickets if t2['contest_id'] == c['contest_id'])` is O(N²) across all tickets and contests. Fine for MVP; group tickets by contest once at the top if you cross ~1000 tickets/user.

rca_of_the_issue: CRITICAL — /api/payments/wallet-topup/custom (£5 valid amount → 500): 1) Reproduction: `POST /api/payments/wallet-topup/custom` with `{amount:5.0, origin_url:'https://example.com'}` and a valid Bearer token. 2) Backend log shows `stripe._error.InvalidRequestError: Invalid line_items[0]: the product tax code is missing. You must set the product's tax_code to one eligible for Managed Payments.` from stripe.checkout.Session.create with managed_payments={enabled: true}. 3) Fallback path (automatic_tax + billing_address_collection) then fails with a similar error: `You must specify a tax code in all line items to calculate taxes.` 4) Legacy /wallet-topup/checkout works because pre-configured Prices already carry the tax code attached in the Stripe dashboard; the custom endpoint uses inline `price_data` with only `currency`, `unit_amount`, and `product_data.name` — no tax code. 5) Fix options: (a) Simplest — add `'tax_code': 'txcd_10103001'` (Digital: Software as a Service) inside `product_data` for both the primary and fallback Session.create calls. (b) Alternatively — drop `managed_payments` + `automatic_tax` for custom sessions and rely on manual tax handling if allowed by SMP rules. (c) Or — mint the Stripe Price server-side once + attach tax_code, then reuse it. Note: the endpoint's Pydantic input validation (`amount: float = Field(..., ge=5.0, le=1000.0)`) correctly returns 422 for out-of-range values, so those tests pass.
